The collaboration addresses the shift from experimental AI deployments to production giga-scale environments requiring unprecedented bandwidth, power, and security controls across the full infrastructure stack.

title: Cisco to Acquire WideField Security to Boost Splunk's Agentic SOC with Identity and Session Intelligence

WideField sessionizes identity signals to distinguish legitimate AI agent activity from potential threats, addressing security risks from authorized AI agents and non-human identities taking unsafe actions faster than human teams can respond. This is Cisco's third AI-focused security acquisition of 2026, following Galileo and Astrix.

title: OpenTelemetry Deprecates OpenCensus Compatibility Requirements in Specification
summary: On June 12, 2026, the OpenTelemetry Specification project merged PR #5138, deprecating OpenCensus compatibility requirements in the specification. This change updates the specification to match where the ecosystem already is: OpenCensus has been archived since July 31, 2023, and the OpenTelemetry shims for OpenCensus have provided a stable migration bridge for more than three years. New SDKs and implementations no longer need to support OpenCensus compatibility; new work should target native OpenTelemetry APIs, SDKs, and OTLP-based workflows instead.

title: OpenAI launches GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, Luna in limited preview with government vetting

summary: On May 21, 2026, OpenTelemetry achieved Graduated status—matching Kubernetes and Prometheus maturity tiers. All three core signals (traces, metrics, logs) are now stable across every major language SDK. This removes the last technical barrier to vendor-neutral observability at scale, with the JavaScript API package alone reaching 1.36 billion downloads per month.

title: OpenTelemetry declarative configuration reaches stable status across five languages
summary: OpenTelemetry's declarative configuration specification stabilized key components: JSON schema, YAML representation, and in-memory data representation. This lets teams configure traces, metrics, and logs in a single YAML file via OTEL_CONFIG_FILE environment variable, eliminating the historical juggling of environment variables, SDK initialization code, and collector configs. Language implementations now available in five languages.

Google CFO acknowledged AI writes approximately 50% of Google's code, while Anthropic stated Claude writes close to 100% of its code.

title: Claude Code June Updates: Stronger Auto-Mode, MCP Reliability, and OpenTelemetry Logging
summary: Claude Code added stronger auto-mode controls, better shell and MCP handling, richer background agent behavior, and improved debugging with new transcript and OpenTelemetry logging. Updates include `/rewind` command to resume conversations before `/clear`, improved MCP reliability and OAuth retries, and CPU use reduction during streaming by approximately 37%.

title: gNMIc Introduces OpenTelemetry Protocol Output Support for Network Telemetry Export
summary: gNMIc added support for OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) as an output destination, enabling direct export of telemetry data to OTLP-compatible backends with full metric conversion (gauges, counters, histograms) and custom resource attributes. The collector command enables dynamic live updates to all configuration objects including targets, subscriptions, outputs, and inputs without requiring restart.

title: Anthropic Claude Agent SDK Credit Split Takes Effect June 15, 2026
summary: On June 15, 2026, the Claude Agent SDK credits system went live, splitting programmatic Claude usage from subscription limits into a separate monthly credit pool billed at standard API rates. Each paid plan received one-time opt-in monthly Agent SDK credit: Pro $20, Max 5x $100, Max 20x $200. Claude Fable 5 suspension due to US export controls required fallback to Opus 4.8 or Sonnet 4.6.

title: Google Reorganizes AI Coding Strike Team to Include Midtraining Strategy After Researcher Departures
summary: Google DeepMind is already reorganizing the AI coding strike team created two months ago, expanding focus to include midtraining rather than concentrating only on coding tools and agents. Midtraining occurs after broad initial training but before final stages that prepare models to follow instructions. The reshuffle comes as Google faces increased competition for AI researchers with Gemini co-lead Noam Shazeer leaving for OpenAI.

title: Anthropic CEO Calls for U.S.-Led AI Coalition at G7 Summit on Standards and Testing
summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis called for a U.S.-led coalition to shape rules and standards around artificial intelligence at a closed-door G7 summit meeting with tech leaders and heads of state including President Trump. The proposal came after Anthropic disabled access to its newest models, Fable 5 and Mythos 5, following U.S. government export control directives citing national security concerns over advanced cyber capabilities.

title: OpenAI Previews GPT-5.6 Series: Sol, Terra, Luna with Government-Mandated Limited Access
summary: OpenAI announced GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna in limited preview, with Sol as the flagship model for frontier reasoning and agentic work. The company is complying with U.S. government request to limit initial rollout to trusted partners. Sol achieves new state-of-the-art on Terminal-Bench 2.1 for coding, improves cybersecurity capabilities, and introduces max reasoning effort and ultra mode using subagents for complex tasks.

title: U.S. Government Authorizes Anthropic to Restore Claude Mythos 5 Access for 100+ Approved Organizations
summary: U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick authorized Anthropic to restore access to Claude Mythos 5 for more than 100 approved U.S. organizations, partially reversing the June 12 export control ban. This follows negotiations between Anthropic and the Trump administration over national security concerns. Claude Fable 5 remains unavailable for general release, with Anthropic continuing discussions for expanded access to both models.

title: Anthropic Alleges Alibaba Used 25,000 Fraudulent Accounts to Analyze Claude Model Capabilities
summary: Anthropic disclosed that a coordinated operation deployed approximately 25,000 fraudulent accounts to interact with Claude, generating over 28 million interactions to extract and analyze the model's reasoning, programming, and task execution capabilities. Alibaba has not publicly responded. The incident highlights emerging supply-chain and competitive intelligence risks in frontier AI model deployment.

title: Singtel Group partners with Digital Industry Singapore to accelerate AI transformation
summary: Singtel Singapore receives up to $28 million from Digital Industry Singapore for a multi-year AI transformation programme covering AI talent, governance, technology architecture, and workforce redesign. The telco's chief AI officer emphasized the need for a single platform because AI agents are expected to spread across customer and network operations, with plans for hundreds or thousands of agents within a year.

title: Telco AI Forum 2026: Operators race to close 6G readiness gap
summary: The global telecom industry's first coordinated AI gathering addressed a critical gap: only 16 percent of telecom generative AI deployments have reached network operations despite years of investment. 3GPP formally confirmed the Release 21 timeline in June 2026, with a Stage-3 protocol freeze in December 2028, creating urgency for domain-specific network AI and autonomous operations.

title: Bell Canada announces 300MW AI data centre in Saskatchewan
summary: Bell Canada and the Government of Saskatchewan announced a 300 MW data centre for Bell AI Fabric, the largest purpose-built AI data centre development in Canada. This represents major investment in sovereign AI infrastructure supporting Bell's enterprise AI services expansion and enabling domestic AI compute capacity.

title: Anthropic's $65B Series H funding round values company at $965B ahead of IPO filing
summary: Anthropic achieved a $965 billion valuation following a $65 billion Series H funding round announced in June 2026 and filed its draft S-1 registration statement on June 1, 2026, positioning it for one of the largest IPOs in stock market history. The funding reflects maturation of large language models from demos to production deployments handling mission-critical workloads, driven by the massive capital requirements for training frontier models that exceed private funding capacity.

title: SpaceX acquires Cursor for $60B; combined entity integrates AI coding platform with Grok training
summary: SpaceX announced its $60 billion all-stock acquisition of Anysphere (Cursor) on June 16, 2026, with closure expected in Q3 2026. Cursor will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary, with Cursor data feeding Grok's training pipeline and a jointly developed model shipping in both Cursor and Grok Build products.

title: EU Parliament approves AI Act amendments: 16-month delay for high-risk AI system compliance
summary: The European Parliament on June 16, 2026 granted final approval to material amendments to the EU AI Act, including delays to high-risk AI system obligations and simplification of regulatory rules. Standalone high-risk AI systems in Annex III categories (education, employment, critical infrastructure) now take effect December 2, 2027 instead of August 2, 2026—a 16-month delay—following sustained industry pressure over compliance guidance availability.

title: Enterprise agentic AI adoption reaches 72% production deployment but governance maturity lags at 21%
summary: Enterprise AI is moving from pilot to production at scale in 2026, yet organizations face critical gaps in governance, talent, and operational readiness. Agentic AI—autonomous systems with minimal human oversight—is poised to grow substantially from 23% current adoption, but only one in five companies has mature governance models for autonomous agents, creating a significant readiness gap.

title: LogicMonitor Publishes AI Workload Observability as Critical ITOps Priority
summary: LogicMonitor published June 17 that AI workload observability helps ITOps teams monitor AI services and reduce blind spots toward Autonomous IT. Edwin AI helps teams move from signal to action by tracking AI workload performance across infrastructure and user experience layers.

title: New Relic Launches AI Coding Observability Open-Source Feature
summary: New Relic released New Relic AI Coding Observability, an open-source observability solution designed for AI-assisted software development. The tool extends production-grade monitoring into the coding phase to govern, optimize, and audit AI usage across the development lifecycle.

title: Dynatrace AI-Guided Troubleshooting Enters Limited Availability with Explainable AI Focus
summary: Chronosphere introduced AI-Guided Troubleshooting capabilities including Suggestions and Investigation Notebooks in limited availability, emphasizing causal reasoning over pattern-spotting. The company plans full general availability in 2026 and released Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server immediately for direct AI workflow integration.

title: New Relic Expands Azure and GitHub Marketplace Integrations at Microsoft Build 2026
summary: New Relic announced double-digit growth in committed bookings through Microsoft Azure Marketplace over the past 12 months. The company positioned observability as agentic AI context for developer workflows and operations agents, integrating deeper with Azure and GitHub Copilot.

title: Data Center Automation: What's New and What Works in 2026
summary: Explores granular, predictive automation across power delivery, cooling, and operations rather than just generative AI. Covers orchestrated electrical power management systems (EPMS) and intelligent PDU coordination for rack-level power capping and workload prioritization in data centers facing electricity constraints.

title: Zscaler Expands Zero Trust SASE With ZAgent Framework for AI-Era Administration
summary: Zscaler introduced the ZAgent framework at Zenith Live 2026 to automate SASE administration and extend zero trust to unmanaged devices, B2B partners, and multi-cloud workloads. The framework uses natural language prompts for management tasks, while automated micro-segmentation within Kubernetes prevents lateral threat movement without code changes. This addresses legacy SASE's firewall/VPN limitations that expose apps and complicate operations in AI-driven threat environments.

title: Zero Trust for AI Agents: SASE Vendors Race to Secure Non-Human Users
summary: SASE providers Versa Networks, Cisco, and Palo Alto are addressing a fundamental shift: agentic AI will introduce non-human identities predicted to outnumber human users by 80-to-1 or higher, but platforms were not built to secure this new class of users. Versa is extending zero-trust to its Verbo agent at the execution layer, ensuring actions are verified with human users before execution. This reflects a strategic pivot across the SASE ecosystem to handle autonomous agent authentication and authorization.

title: Zscaler Announces AI-Guardian Project and Platform Integrations for Enterprise AI Security
summary: Zscaler announced new AI- and agent-focused capabilities with integrations with Oasis Security, Radiant Logic, and Gigamon to strengthen identity governance and observability across complex hybrid environments. The announcements at Zenith Live 2026 demonstrate vendor consolidation around identity governance and observability as critical foundations for securing distributed AI workloads and agents within zero-trust architectures.

title: Honeycomb Releases Second Edition of Observability Engineering for AI-First Operations
summary: Honeycomb announced the second edition of 'Observability Engineering: Achieving Production Excellence,' updated to reflect that AI agents are now both producers and consumers of observability data in production systems. The revised edition, co-authored by founder Charity Majors with Austin Parker (Director of AI Strategy), addresses how observability platforms must be designed for autonomous agent reasoning and debugging.

title: AI-Native 6G Momentum Building at EuCNC Summit: Agentic AI Integration with Standards Framework
summary: Nokia reported findings from EuCNC & 6G Summit 2026 showing accelerating momentum toward AI-native 6G architectures. Key result: agentic AI will be seamlessly integrated into 6G systems, balancing interoperability requirements from standards bodies (3GPP, ETSI) with practical AI innovations. Commercial deployment timeline remains 2030, but research-to-implementation gap is narrowing significantly.

title: AutoCon 5: Network Automation Forum Convenes 200+ Practitioners on AI-Driven Infrastructure Reliability
summary: Packet Pushers covered AutoCon 5 (June 6-10, 2026) in Munich, where network operators and architects discussed SRE, AI-driven infrastructure automation, network monitoring tools, and code-based traffic management. Keynote: 'The SRE of AI: Engineering Network Reliability for the Tokenized Era,' focusing on maintaining service levels and managing distributed systems under AI workloads.

title: Zscaler Expands Zero Trust SASE with ZAgent Framework for AI-Era Security Operations
summary: Zscaler announced significant expansion of its Zero Trust SASE solution with introduction of ZAgent Framework, an orchestration system designed to automate administrative tasks such as configuration and troubleshooting. Administrators interact with the system using natural language prompts. The expansion includes Zero Trust Gateway for GCP, automated microsegmentation for Kubernetes environments to restrict lateral threat movement, and Zero Trust browser options for BYOD devices.

title: Fortinet Introduces FortiSOC: Unified Cloud-Delivered SOC Platform with Agentic AI
summary: Fortinet held exclusive webinar on June 17, 2026 introducing FortiSOC, a new unified, cloud-delivered SOC platform designed to simplify and scale modern security operations. Platform consolidates alert management and automates response workflows using agentic AI, addressing SOC teams' struggle with manual investigation and response processes.

title: FortiBleed: 73,932 Fortinet Firewalls Compromised via Configuration Exfiltration and Credential Hash Cracking
summary: Security researcher Bob Diachenko discovered FortiBleed, a large-scale credential compromise affecting 73,932 Fortinet FortiGate VPN firewalls across 194 countries. Threat actors extracted configuration files from internet-exposed devices, cracked password hashes using 45-GPU clusters via Hashtopolis, and assembled validated credential database. Campaign included 1.16 billion login attempts against FortiGate targets and 2.1 billion attempts against MSSQL servers, impacting organizations including Samsung, Foxconn, Comcast, and AT&T.
